summary: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists an Apple Springs tower in Trinity County as gone; no source read gives its build date, height or site today.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association's Texas list marks it gone.

evidence.supports: Community is fifteen miles northeast of Groveton, in northeastern Trinity County
evidence.quote: fifteen miles northeast of Groveton in northeastern Trinity County

evidence.supports: Community established after the Civil War, first called May Apple Springs
evidence.quote: The community was established after the Civil War and was originally known as May Apple Springs

evidence.supports: Post office opened in 1884 and the name was shortened
evidence.quote: When a post office opened in 1884 the name was shortened to Apple Springs

evidence.supports: Town moved to State Highway 94 after the railroad was abandoned in 1931
evidence.quote: When the railroad was abandoned in 1931, the town was moved to State Highway 94

evidence.supports: Texas list entry: Apple Springs, Trinity County, coordinates, tower, gone
Trinity CCC camp: fifty men arrived in Trinity on May 26, 1933
evidence.quote: On May 26, 1933, fifty men under the command of Captain Charles H. Brammel arrived in Trinity

evidence.supports: CCC members worked on fire lanes, fire towers and fire break roads in Trinity, Houston and Walker counties
evidence.quote: Members participated in erosion prevention, construction and maintenance of fire lanes, fire towers, and fire break roads in Trinity, Houston and Walker counties

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The full HMDB marker text was checked and does not contain the word Apple, so the 'marker does not mention' sentence stands. The story now footnotes the May Apple Springs sentence. The tower appears only as a row in the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Texas list (Trinity County, coordinates, gone). The community and CCC marker are context. No source read ties the Trinity CCC camp's fire-tower work to the Apple Springs tower, and the story says the marker does not name it. The listed coordinates were not checked against any site description. No build date, height, staffing or current-site description found. Two searches and about five page reads used.
